name: Evelyn Wade
life: “I still remember covering a colleague's train fare during a strike.” On Saturday, near Paper & Pine Books, Evelyn starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I have savings. I promised to cover a day's wages for the youngest worker if she wanted to speak.
appearance: Evelyn is easy to recognize by short black hair swept back and one cheek that creases before the other. Usually dressed in a faded indigo overshirt with a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it, Evelyn looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry when listening.
personality: Evelyn listens for the familiar version of a story and then for the one detail that changes it. Friends bring problems here when they want to be heard twice.
agenda: To cover the youngest speaker's lost day.
family: Dario Allard is Evelyn’s younger cousin. Their family had a rule about visiting someone who had fallen on hard times. Bring enough food for the next day and bring a reason for an ordinary conversation. Evelyn can rustle up a convincing practical excuse for a visit. Asked about *The spare spectacles*, Dario says, “I keep my dad's spare pair in my bag to see menus the way he did.”
connections: Chris Moss. Sales figures give the worker financing a colleague's absence a better bargaining position.
